title: MasOrange, Ericsson test 6 GHz spectrum in early step toward 6G future
summary: MasOrange and Ericsson successfully tested the 6 GHz band, a leading candidate for future 6G networks, validating advanced antenna technologies that could quadruple network capacity while supporting AI-driven services, digital twins and next-generation automation.

title: Elliott pushes Deutsche Telekom to prioritize buybacks over T-Mobile US mega-merger
summary: Elliott Investment Management is urging Germany’s Deutsche Telekom (DT) to back off a potential mega-merger plan with DT’s U.S.-based T-Mobile, according to reports.

title: Jan Hofmeyr named DT's new Board of Management member for product and technology
summary: Hofmeyr hails from AWS where he was VP of Telecom. He replaces Abdu Mudesir who left to take the role of EVP & President of Global Networks, Platforms & Technology.

title: Orange acquires Obvios’ Dome private 5G core technology
summary: Orange is deepening its sovereign connectivity play with private 5G core tech aimed at defense, public safety and critical infrastructure customers.

title: Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face in $12.9B AI infrastructure deal
summary: Nvidia’s planned $12.9B Hugging Face acquisition could reshape the open-source AI ecosystem, giving the AI chip giant deeper control over a key platform for models, datasets and developer tools while raising questions about openness, competition and enterprise AI deployment.

title: Broadcom predicts AI chip revenue to double in 2027
summary: Broadcom's third quarter 2026 earnings were strong, driven by accelerating demand for its AI chips.

title: AI agents expose 5G core security risks for telecom operators
summary: AI agents found dozens of previously unknown flaws in 4G and 5G cores, underscoring why telecom operators and vendors can no longer treat internal network interfaces as automatically trusted.

title: T-Mobile taps former Shell CFO Jessica Uhl to help steer next phase of AI and enterprise growth
summary: Uhl's background in large-scale infrastructure investments, corporate development and AI initiatives could prove valuable as T-Mobile pursues opportunities across enterprise and emerging AI-driven services.

title: NTIA decides BEAD non-deployment funds can be used for deployment
summary: After NTIA favored cheap satellite technology over fiber broadband, the BEAD fund of $42.5 billion was left with $21 billion in left-over monies.

title: SK Telecom's AI model push offers a blueprint for telcos seeking sovereignty
summary: SK Telecom’s approach shows how telcos can use models to gain more control over AI deployments and put model ownership at the center of their AI strategy.

title: Ciena’s biggest problem is keeping up with the demand for its optical products
summary: While Ciena's Q3 2026 revenue numbers all looked good, the company’s stock has dropped about 10%. Fierce spoke with Ciena’s Chief Strategy Officer and asked why.

title: Opinion: In a UK drought, who gets to drink?
summary: U.K. government policy still does not clearly say who takes priority when there's not enough water to go round.

title: Here's one fiber network builder who doesn't leave communities behind
summary: While some hyperscalers won't build fiber off-ramps to towns and cities that its fiber passes on the way to data centers, Light Source does the opposite.

title: Studies say: Mobile carriers can chill – satellites can’t go it alone
summary: Based on recent studies and a WIA panel discussion, one could reasonably conclude that terrestrial mobile networks will survive – even though popular perception says Elon Musk’s SpaceX will obliterate them.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise reports 3Q results
summary: Networking revenue was $2.9 billion, up 74.9% from the prior-year period, with 22.0% operating profit margin, compared to 22.1% from the prior-year period.

title: AI boom through 2050 hinges on power supply, politics, PwC says
summary: AI may unleash a $31.6 trillion data center buildout by 2050, but PwC says the real race isn’t just for capital — it’s for power, chips and political advantages.

title: Opinion: Huawei: They may rip out our networks, but they'll never take our patents!
summary: The announcement last week of an IP licensing agreement between HP and Huawei is significant, but perhaps not for the reason most people imagine.

title: Equinix and CPP Investments close $4B atNorth acquisition
summary: The deal nets Equinix and CPP eight data centers in the five nordic countries, as well as new facilities under development.

title: Engineers craft 6G. It’s marketers' job to sell it
summary: Can the wireless industry separate the standards from a consumer-facing approach and quit its reliance on the next “G” to shape its messaging?

title: GAO recommends FCC and NTIA take actions to aid broadband programs
summary: GAO wrote that local governments, tribes and industry associations reported difficulties with the bulk challenge process as part of the FCC's broadband map.

title: Calix names Juergen Lindner as CMO
summary: Juergen brings deep expertise in product, go-to-market, and business transformation as Calix extends the value of its AI-native platform for service providers and adjacent markets.

title: AI enters cost crunch era as hyperscalers zero in on affordability, controls
summary: Enterprises are waking up to AI’s runaway costs, pushing hyperscalers to pitch affordability alongside performance.

title: Helium pitches its playbook to carriers, MVNOs and brands
summary: Helium CEO Mario Di Dio says the industry is moving toward a more distributed, usage-based connectivity model that spans cellular, Wi-Fi and satellite.

title: AWS and Microsoft launch multicloud networking in preview
summary: AWS to Azure connectivity is now available in preview in four Microsoft cloud regions, with plans to expand.

title: Charter’s CFO departs; AT&T sues Charter for false advertising
summary: AT&T's lawsuit claims that Charter’s advertising for its broadband service uses words such as “fiber powered” to deceptively suggest a fiber-to-the-home service.
